label: Enable installed low-voltage hardware
help: Off by default. Only buttons and indicator LEDs with correct current limiting; never mains, power relays or safety-critical devices.

label: GPIO chip device
help: Exact /dev/gpiochipN from the installed board. Offsets below are chip line offsets, not physical header pin numbers.

label: Button line offset
help: -1 disables the button. Choose an unused input line and verify the board pinout before enabling.

label: LED line offset
help: -1 disables the LED. Must differ from the button. Use a resistor and respect the board's voltage/current ratings.

label: Button active low
help: Checked means a low electrical level is a press. Startup and resume establish a baseline; they do not invent a press.

label: Button pull resistor
help: Internal bias is best effort in Linux. Provide the required external bias; a floating input is not reliable.

label: Stable level before event (ms)
help: Emit only after the sampled level remains stable. Held buttons do not repeat; very short pulses may be missed.

label: LED active low
help: Checked means logical on drives a low electrical level. Verify the circuit; this does not change the supply voltage.

label: LED on at rest / before release
help: Applied at acquisition, after timed patterns and before release. After release or power loss the circuit, not this block, determines the level.

label: Maximum LED command duration (ms)
help: Every on command needs duration_ms. Blink count and complete duration are bounded. A new accepted command replaces the current pattern.

label: Maximum button events per Run
help: Releases the lines at this limit. Pause/resume does not reset the total; start a new Run.

label: Button sampling interval (ms)
help: Ordinary human buttons, not pulse counting or real-time control. Scheduling delays can miss short transitions.

label: libgpiod library (administrator)
help: Normally libgpiod.so.3 (API 2.x). An absolute .so path loads native code: only use a trusted installed library.
